learningObjectives.title: Nazi dictatorship and life in Nazi Germany

questions.q: On what date did Kaiser Wilhelm II abdicate, opening the way for the Weimar Republic?
questions.explain: The Kaiser abdicated on 9 November 1918, two days before the armistice ended the First World War.

questions.q: Which article of the Weimar Constitution allowed the President to rule by emergency decree?
questions.explain: Article 48 let the President suspend civil rights and rule by decree in an emergency, a power later exploited by the Nazis.

questions.q: Why was proportional representation often seen as a weakness of the Weimar system?
options: It led to many small parties and unstable coalition governments
It gave the President the power to ban elections
It stopped women from being able to vote
It handed all power to a single party
questions.explain: Proportional representation meant even tiny parties won seats, producing fragile coalitions that frequently collapsed.

questions.q: The Treaty of Versailles limited the German army to how many men?
questions.explain: The treaty capped the German army at 100,000 men and also banned conscription, tanks, submarines and an air force.

questions.q: What did Article 231 of the Treaty of Versailles, the 'war guilt clause', require Germany to do?
options: Accept blame for causing the First World War
Give up all of its colonies
questions.explain: Article 231 forced Germany to accept responsibility for the war, which was used to justify reparations and caused deep resentment.

questions.q: Which new currency did Stresemann introduce in late 1923 to help end hyperinflation?
questions.explain: Stresemann replaced the worthless paper mark with the Rentenmark in November 1923, restoring confidence in the currency.

questions.q: How did the Dawes Plan of 1924 help the Weimar Republic recover?
options: It provided US loans and rescheduled reparation payments
It cancelled all of Germany's reparations for good
It permanently removed French troops from the Rhineland
It expelled Germany from the League of Nations
questions.explain: The Dawes Plan spread out reparation payments and brought in American loans, helping the German economy stabilise.

questions.q: In which year did Hitler and the Nazis attempt the Munich (Beer Hall) Putsch?
questions.explain: The failed Munich Putsch took place in November 1923, after which Hitler was imprisoned and wrote Mein Kampf.

questions.q: On what date was Hitler appointed Chancellor of Germany by President Hindenburg?
questions.explain: Hindenburg appointed Hitler Chancellor on 30 January 1933, persuaded by Papen who believed he could be controlled.

questions.q: Why did support for the Nazi Party grow so rapidly after 1929?
options: Mass unemployment in the Depression made extreme parties more attractive
The Nazis had already won a majority in the 1928 election
Stresemann had banned all rival parties
Hyperinflation had wiped out savings once again
questions.explain: The Wall Street Crash triggered the Depression and mass unemployment, driving desperate voters towards the Nazis and other extremes.

questions.q: How did Hitler use the Reichstag Fire of February 1933 to strengthen his position?
options: He blamed the communists and passed a decree removing civil liberties
He resigned as Chancellor to appear moderate
He rebuilt the Reichstag as a Nazi monument
He formed an alliance with the SPD
questions.explain: Hitler blamed the communists and used the fire to pass the Reichstag Fire Decree, suspending civil rights and arresting opponents.

questions.q: What did the Enabling Act of March 1933 allow Hitler to do?
options: Make laws for four years without the consent of the Reichstag
Disband the SA and the SS
questions.explain: The Enabling Act let Hitler pass laws without the Reichstag, effectively ending parliamentary democracy in Germany.

questions.q: In June 1934 Hitler ordered the murder of Ernst Röhm and other SA leaders. What was his main aim?
options: To remove the SA threat and win the loyalty of the army
To punish the communists for the Reichstag Fire
To take revenge for the failed Munich Putsch
questions.explain: The Night of the Long Knives destroyed the SA's power and reassured the army, which then swore an oath to Hitler after Hindenburg's death.

questions.q: Who was the Nazi Minister of Propaganda?
questions.explain: Goebbels controlled propaganda, censorship, the press, radio and rallies to promote the Nazi message and the Hitler myth.

questions.q: In 1936 a German-Jewish couple find they can no longer vote and are forbidden to marry a non-Jew. Which Nazi measure caused this?
questions.explain: The 1935 Nuremberg Laws stripped Jews of German citizenship and banned marriage between Jews and non-Jews.

questions.q: What was Kristallnacht of November 1938?
options: A nationwide attack on Jewish homes, shops and synagogues
A one-day boycott of Jewish businesses in 1933
The opening of the first concentration camp
A law removing Jews from the professions
questions.explain: During Kristallnacht, Jewish property and synagogues were destroyed across Germany and many Jews were killed or arrested.

questions.q: Which statement best describes the Nazi view of the role of women?
options: They promoted 'Kinder, Küche, Kirche', focusing women on children, home and church
They encouraged women to take senior factory and management jobs
They gave women equal political rights for the first time
They banned women from marrying or having children
questions.explain: Nazi policy encouraged women to leave work and raise large families, rewarding motherhood with schemes like the Mother's Cross.

questions.q: Who led the SS, the organisation that ran the police, camps and terror system?
questions.explain: Himmler headed the SS, which grew to control the Gestapo, concentration camps and the wider Nazi terror apparatus.

questions.q: A German worker is offered cheap holidays, cinema trips and sports through a state leisure scheme. Which Nazi organisation provided these?
questions.explain: Strength Through Joy (Kraft durch Freude) offered subsidised leisure to keep workers loyal and content under the regime.

questions.q: In 1933 the Nazis signed the Concordat with the Pope. What did Hitler gain from this agreement?
options: Catholic recognition of the regime in return for promised religious freedom
The complete abolition of the Catholic Church in Germany
Control over the League of Nations
The backing of the German Communist Party
questions.explain: The Concordat had the Catholic Church stay out of politics and accept the Nazi state in exchange for freedom of worship, boosting Hitler's legitimacy.

specSource: Pearson Edexcel International GCSE History (4HI1) specification; Germany: Development of Dictatorship 1918-45
